verdict:
Pages 4-6: 10 of the 13 findings are fully fixed and match the code changes. Two are fixed with small leftovers: page 4's caption block still grazes the lamp at 87.80, and page 6's steel pile still reaches into the right button strip at full size. One is only partly fixed: page 5's stray YEN callout leader was moved 0.5 s earlier, not removed. A render at 100.85 still shows a bare orange line ending on the red cloth before the stack has landed.

The page 4 must-fix is properly solved. A 0.22 s / 0.26 s dip on 'homes' (92.20) hides the board, notice, stamp and strikers, and the site shot opens clean.

Page 5's top-hat cut-out is gone, and the right tower grows clearly taller, as the lead decided. But the coins never visibly come to rest on it. The camera is below the tower top and early coins are buried under later bundles, so they only fall past it and vanish.

Page 6's notes now land face-up and read as money. The output pile sits centre-right and shrinks visibly. The racing counter no longer settles on a number, but its doubled 'ghost' digits look like a render glitch.

Page turns at 94.70, 128.02 and 155.54 (joins-d) are clean. No words break the section 5 rules, and every hook matches the narration at its time.

Should-fix before sign-off:
1. Re-time the page 5 YEN callout to about T.creates+0.6.
2. Make the page 5 coin pour visibly land and pile up.

verdict: Most findings on pages 7-10 are fixed, but not all of them, and the fixes caused two new problems. Fixed: COSTS and SOMETIMES on page 7, the $2.90 hold and the A BARREL plate; the 'lowest on record' caption, the house plinth and the $ tag on page 8; the WAGES packet and the coin stack on page 9; the 5.6% hold, the dial label, the upright quote, the capitalised words and the credits on page 10. New must-fix on page 8: the latest close-up camera pushes the FLAT OUT callout off screen, so 'flat out' (186.7 s) has no words on screen. My still at 186.95 and the lead's 187.3/187.9 stills confirm it. Partly fixed on page 10: the needle no longer slides during the unemployment beat, but it now visibly falls from 5.5 to 2.25 while she says 'the Reserve Bank is raising' (255.5-257.2 s, confirmed in my 256.60 still). Page 8's board still clips at the right edge during the 188.2-188.8 s pan. On page 9 the weight is partly hidden behind a queue figure. The page-3 half of the price-board finding was not checked here.
